The WHO Country Cooperation Strategy (CCS) is a medium-term corporate strategic framework designed to address the priorities of the Thirteenth General Programme of Work (GPW13). It identifies key priorities for technical cooperation with Member States, taking into account national contexts, and facilitates coordination with United Nations Country Teams and other partners. The CCS guides dialogue, priority setting, and implementation of WHO’s work at the country level to achieve the “triple billion” targets and health-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The CCS provides a step-by-step guide for developing each chapter of the strategy and includes key checklists. Mid-term and final evaluations of the CCS will assess the implementation of priorities through the country support plan and the achievement of targets and indicators from the WHO impact framework. The CCS serves as a strategic vision for public health impacts and outcomes, supporting the implementation of GPW13 at the country level and monitoring results. It outlines WHO’s agreed priorities and their alignment with national contexts and needs, including the health and development agenda. It also highlights opportunities for collaboration and interaction among various partners and stakeholders. The CCS promotes country ownership in achieving health-related SDGs by negotiating, agreeing, endorsing, and monitoring priorities through senior government and WHO officials. It also provides a platform for increasing WHO’s visibility in terms of communication and advocacy, drawing attention to WHO’s work with specific Member States and enhancing opportunities for resource mobilization. The CCS is aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and serves as a starting point for WHO’s work in a country. It ensures strategic coherence, complementarity, and coordination among UN entities with mandates relevant to health, boosting the standing of health in the development agenda. It also serves as a tool for mobilizing resources at the country level and demonstrating support for global and regional health agendas. The CCS is a public product that enhances the visibility and accountability of WHO operations and results. Unlike internal planning tools, it can be used for external communication, resource mobilization, and advocacy for priority issues in the country. It also contributes to WHO’s transparency in the responsible use of international aid, as demonstrated by its participation in the International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI). The CCS development process facilitates broad dialogue and strengthens partnerships based on the country’s full national health and development agenda. It provides a clear strategic rationale for WHO’s work, guiding planning processes and setting out WHO’s role and contribution to the UN system at the country level. It promotes country ownership in achieving health-related SDGs and goes beyond measuring WHO outcomes and impact by focusing on the country’s progress toward joint priorities and impact targets. The CCS is a practical toolkit that provides a step-by-step approach to developing a concise and evidence-based strategy. It assists all stakeholders involved in the process, ensuring alignment with GPW13 and UNSDCF, and serves as a mechanism for strategic coherence and coordination among partners.
